script.title: Finding One: The Door Is Lying
script.synopsis: At 2 a.m. the Inspector investigates why a fridge door alarm keeps beeping and a phone lead keeps slipping out of the socket. She blames the door and the socket while an off-camera flatmate asks what the noise is. When the beam finds the phone inside the fridge, she is the culprit. She solves the door problem with a milk carton wedge and delivers 'Under review' with one clipboard tap while the beep continues.

beats.beat: Phone on a taut lead in the open fridge, door drifts, plug slips, beep, 'the door is lying'
She presses the plug home, the door drifts, beeps speed up
Flatmate asks what the noise is while her beam slides onto her own phone
She wedges the door with the carton; the flatmate asks why the phone is in the fridge

scenes.location: Shared kitchen at 2 a.m., in front of the open fridge beside the wall socket
scenes.action: Locked in on the open fridge: the Inspector stands behind the door as a dark silhouette, chest lamp a white disc on the middle shelf where the phone lies between butter dish and jar, lead stretched taut to the socket. The door drifts shut by a hand's width, the plug eases one centimetre out of the socket and a single beep sounds. She turns her head to the door and whispers her finding.
scenes.performance: Invested task: she is verifying the door's behaviour like a witness statement; her eyes travel from the door edge to the plug and back, jaw still, breath held between words.
scenes.microexpression: Brows stay level; a slow blink as the beep lands.

continuity.identity_anchors: Oval face, straight dark brows, small round glasses pushed slightly down the nose, neutral expression that breaks into warm disappointment rather than anger.
continuity.costume: Aubergine utility jacket with four flap pockets, bright circular inspection lamp on a chest strap, tiny clipboard on a lanyard (worn, not a moving prop), hair in a tight low bun.
props: plain milk carton on the top of the fridge door shelf
continuity.notes: Exactly two props move: the phone (stays on the middle shelf throughout, charging when the plug seats) and the plain milk carton (taken from the door shelf in S4 to wedge the door). The fridge door and the plug are fixtures, not props; the door and plug move only as the fixture's own behaviour. Butter dish, jar, socket, lead and the clipboard on its lanyard are set dressing/worn costume. The flatmate is never seen and the only light sources are the fridge light and the chest lamp. No readable brand text; no cable ties or wrapped cable, no cordon tape, cones or tick-counting; the clipboard tap occurs once, in S5.
